note: Reconstitution of Enniskillen rural district council. Twenty-three Unionist candidates were nominated for the twenty-six divisions and, there being no Nationalist nominations, were returned unopposed; no candidates came forward for three divisions (Belfast News-Letter, 24 April 1924). The News-Letter's list names twenty-two of the twenty-three; the twenty-third, Drummee (Wm. J. Brown, J.P.), is read from the Fermanagh Herald's list (26 April 1924, p. 5). The three divisions without a candidate (Kinawley, Oldbar, Holywell) had no retiring member to be deemed re-elected in this reconstituted council and fell to be filled by the council as casual vacancies (County and Rural District Councillors (NI) Election Order 1924, r. 10 proviso); co-options are not election results. Unopposed Unionist nomination. Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Coolyermor' to Coolyermer (19 Nov 2026, w19-tidy, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the 1911 DED map (Enniskillen Rural District) and the Northern Ireland DED maps of 1921-69 name the DED Coolyermer; the rounds were filed as Coolyermor (1924, 1930, 1933, 1936, 1939, 1946, 1949, 1955, 1958, 1961); Cooleyermor (1927); Coolyermer (1952); Coolyermore (1964). This round was filed as 'Coolyermor', kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (coolyermor) answers with a redirect to this one.
